short: 38-phoneme intracortical classification (M06) is standard: new for intracranial signals, prior in ultrasound and EMG; one participant, bins split at random into folds.
position: The paper [@brumberg2011classification] changes one component, the decoder (M06): it replaces the same participant's continuous three-vowel formant control [@guenther2009] with discrete classification of 38 attempted phonemes, a class set that none of the 3 prior intracranial ledger studies uses (pattern match, Appendix); the largest read prior intracranial set was ten overt words [@kellis2010decoding]. It is standard, not ahead: full phone sets were already the units of phone recognition from tongue ultrasound and lip video [@hueber2008phone] and from EMG of silent speech [@walliczek2006subword] (Appendix), and nothing repeats the result beyond one participant with five pooled sessions. The evaluation (M12) is standard for 2011, but its samples are 300-ms bins assigned to folds at random, with no statement that a trial's 20 bins share a fold: the strongest confound for the 16–21% accuracies. "Intended" rests on an instruction and a post-trial denial check, with no attempt onset. The authors' conclusion that the rates are "truly not great enough to be useful as a communication device" holds; their reading of them as "a conservative, lower-bound" does not, because a trial-mixed split biases upward (inference).
